questions.stem: What happens to a protein when it is denatured?

options.text: Its 3D shape changes permanently so it can no longer function
Its peptide bonds are broken and amino acids are released

questions.explanation: When a protein is denatured, the bonds maintaining its tertiary structure (hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, disulfide bridges) are broken, changing its 3D shape. The active site or binding site no longer fits its substrate, so it loses its function.
